Definition: from G4314 and G2064 (including its alternate); to approach, i.e. (literally) come near, visit, or (figuratively) worship, assent to:--(as soon as he) come (unto), come thereunto, consent, draw near, go (near, to, unto).
BiblicalUsage: Proserchomai means to come near, to approach, to draw close. A leper came and worshipped Jesus, saying, Lord, if Thou wilt, Thou canst make me clean. Hebrews says, Let us come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need, and, Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith. And without faith it is impossible to please God, for he that cometh to God must believe that He is.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe coming near is the whole of the Christian life: the leper came and was cleansed, and I come and find mercy. I hold that boldness is not presumption when the way was opened by blood, and faith is simply the coming itself, trusting that God is there and that He rewards those who seek Him.
